how: Different members propose locations, report an initial build and call for a new figure, distributing starting across several projects.
A stated pixel delay motivates gathering many placers, with further calls recruiting help through ordinary discussion.
Recruitment includes explaining the unfamiliar canvas to newcomers, including readers who encounter it after building has begun.
Participants propose national and local images, revise the crest and borders, and dispute visual legibility and additions.
Reports identify an initial flag, a larger build and the shift from a completed figure to flag making.
Coordinates, a template instruction and exact border thickness align placing while corrections remain open.
Detailed coordination moves into chat while public thread instructions and proposals continue alongside it.
Making turns explicitly into maintenance, constant camping and redesign against tampering.
Members distinguish attackers from flag makers and disclaim control over every participant, while later testimony includes admitted internal sabotage.
Attributions identify participants' explanations rather than independently verified placers, including a conspiracy claim that cannot establish authorship.
Members demand returned space, reject destructive expansion and prioritize maintaining existing work.
Neighbour agreements specify moves, overlap and coexistence, with later appeals holding placers to an existing agreement.
Converting a neighbour's flag and calling to erase or cover other works are visible, without establishing universal adoption of those calls.
Calls posted after placement stopped show attempted mobilization rather than executable new attacks.
Relocation is observed for the injured neighbour whose maker says the sign displaced its work and later confirms a successful move.
Members announce completion, claim shared overnight labour and report personal time invested in the work.
Celebration marks a temporary achieved state and can be answered immediately by renewed damage rather than ending upkeep.
Final-state reporting prompts mourning, retrospective explanations and corrections about whether placement remains possible.
A replacement canvas is proposed and explicitly declined, making continuation a decision under consideration rather than an accomplished persistence.
The earlier shared-flag proposal concerns the original open canvas, so it cannot itself evidence carrying the effort beyond closure.
Destructive alternate accounts are alleged, while subsequent beard work does not confirm their use or establish a shared automation programme.
Rebuilding calls and progress reports receive short commitments that ask for nothing in return.
Requested assistance becomes reported placing, completed repair and thanks that explicitly restore the injured neighbour's trust.
A participant recalls a heart made jointly with another national group, supporting joint work without establishing a standing coalition or shared defensive command.
The contest extends into a posted declaration of war and a disputed claim about converting an abandoned flag.
Saying another country's canvas effort is going badly supports comparison, not a victory claim or evidence that the speaker defeated it.
Overlap proposals and an agreement do not establish a host exercising rule over guests, leaving host-governed accommodation unobserved.
Members object to the volume and value of canvas talk by proposing filtering, welcoming other posts and criticizing expansion fatigue.
Disclaiming practical control over every placer is visible, but it does not establish a dispute over the negotiator's authority to agree.
A cleaned representation is inspected and faulted, but no concept establishes a dispute over preserving damage as history rather than correcting it.
April Fools appears through greetings, distrust and moderator jokes without establishing a staged takeover or blanket licence for canvas aggression.
One participant judges the available hands insufficient and proposes joining the void, while a reply challenges that stance.
National attack calls do not state an established pre-canvas quarrel, leaving the importation of a prior dispute unobserved.
National history and familiar local lines supply jokes for relocation, restraint, defence and negotiation.
Visible instructions and a sanction with an obscured trigger cannot establish the room's absence of decided canvas order or test the model's comparative prevalence claim.
An unexplained moderator cool-off cannot be classified as excluding canvas vandals or enforcing a decided canvas order.
Naming a national target in an attack call does not by itself establish a prior tie or historical motive for that attack.
A participant carries an agreed three-pixel move into the neighbouring thread without evidence of formal appointment.
A request for help leads through location guidance to a reported larger build and a promise to click.
The member who calls for a new figure immediately reports the starting portion, supporting a local starter-and-call sequence.
The explicit instruction that the flag now only needs maintenance supports the transition from made work to upkeep.
Negotiation also answers damage attributed to the room's own expansion, rather than arising only from erosion of its own work.
A participant explicitly invokes an existing agreement as the reason to return occupied neighbour space, without establishing that restitution occurred.
Upkeep and alternate accounts are visible, but the observed alt dispute does not show defensive shortage causing machine escalation.
A neighbour's report of successful relocation is directly answered by collective celebration.
A celebration post supplies the occasion for a reply presenting the work's hours compressed into a short recording.
A final recording and replacement-canvas invitation occur, but no cited turn makes recording the cause of continuation and the visible response declines it.
The insufficient-hands judgment receives disagreement rather than an observable relocation decision, while the documented later move concerns a different injured work.
Template-following and design criticism coexist, but the coded record does not show a posted template resolving the design disagreement.
A rebuilding appeal receives a short acceptance without a request for return assistance.
Bare refusal also occurs, so reply brevity cannot determine acceptance or establish that a declining member supplies a reason.
Cross-room help also follows an injured neighbour's resource shortage and displacement, without evidence that the helpers themselves ran short of hands.
Relocation agreement and placement negotiation accompany rebuilding reports and a commitment to help.
Recruitment and attack proposals share a thread, but the concepts do not establish that the recruitment turned particular participants into attackers.
An attack proposal receives a reasoned preference for joint making and a separate explicit rejection of the proposed attacker.
Negotiation follows a target's explicit complaint about destruction, while the coded exchange does not identify an initiating attack call.
The author of an attack proposal reports posting a declaration of war in the named rival's subreddit.
Recollection of a jointly made heart does not establish that shared attack pressure caused coalition formation.
An expansion call receives a reply welcoming closure because expansion posts have become tiresome, supporting member resistance to canvas talk.
A practical control disclaimer accompanies negotiation, leaving any claim that agreements provoked a dispute over representatives' authority unresolved.
An unnamed meme and its claimed drawers cannot securely instantiate finding or representing the room's canvas mark because the event connection remains uncertain.

statement: Carrying on ordinary room talk beside canvas work
how: An ordinary subreddit redirect remains local conversational residue without supplying evidence of canvas organizing or coordination migration.
